newsitem.title: USA: Saxton says US deficit could fall below $100 bln.
newsitem.headline: Saxton says US deficit could fall below $100 bln.

text.p: Joint Economic Committee Chairman Jim Saxton said Tuesday the U.S. budget deficit could fall below $100 billion in 1997 due to strong economic growth.

The Treasury Monday said during the first six months of fiscal 1997 that ends on Sept. 30, the cumulative budget deficit dropped 13 percent to $111.28 billion from $127.71 billion in the comparable first six months of fiscal 1996.

"The sustained economic expansion continues to boost revenues and hold down spending growth," Saxton said. "The possibility of deficit spending falling below $100 billion is very encouraging," the New Jersey Republican added.
There has been some discussion that the Congressional Budget Office will revise downward its budget deficit projection for 1997 to below $100 billion from its most recent estimate of $112 billion.

The Clinton administration has forecast a deficit for fiscal 1997 of $126 billion, up from a deficit in fiscal 1996 of $107 billion. Lawrence Haas, spokesman for the White House Office of Management and Budget, said the administration had no plans at this time to revise its deficit estimate. The next time an official deficit projection would be released would be in the summer, he said.
"We will have a better sense of whether we're truly ahead of schedule when the April receipts come in," Haas added.
